q1_issues.issue: "crumble" is a verb of internal change of state, whose intransitive subject the role test assigns Patient rather than Agent - salt-bloom undergoes the crumbling, it does not do it.

q2_gaps: A bare MASS-noun subject in a verbal generic ("Iron makes salt-bloom crumble"): the verbal-generic doctrine mandates a distributing rule for a kind subject but illustrates only bare plurals, while Status predicates says a status-free event is already the generic/habitual reading - nothing settles which form a bare-mass-subject generic takes, or whether its atoms then fall under the empirical 0.9 confidence dial.

The periphrastic-causative rule states flatly that a bare-infinitive complement makes the object the caused event's Agent (its example verb is the volitional "sprint"), which collides with the intransitive-subject role test when the complement verb is a change-of-state verb such as crumble/collapse/melt.
notes: The rest of the causative frame is right: matrix make event, causer as Agent, caused event as Theme, the object living only inside the caused event, and salt_bloom's compound genus. If the generic reading is the intended one, the 0.99 confidences would drop to the empirical 0.9.
